finalText:
**Found the leak in `src/jobs/processOrder.js` and fixed it.**

It called `pool.acquire()`, then `await run(...)`, then `pool.release(conn)`. When an order rejected, the release line never ran. A comment said it acquired directly because the connection had to be held across a retry loop, but that loop was already gone. It now uses `withConnection`, which releases in a `finally`.

The logs match exactly. `worker.log` has 125 job starts and 120 releases, and 5 of the 7 failures were real leaks — the other two already hit an empty pool. The pool holds 5, so the 5th bad order at `02:06:30` filled it, and `worker-1` died three seconds later.

The app process leaked the same way through `POST /orders`, which is why 503s and the supervisor restart follow at `02:11`. `handleRequest` was already safe.

All 4 tests pass, 68ms.
